The complete app source

Inspect, build or modify the code used for this release. The ZIP includes application code, checks, build instructions, vendored SMB libraries and their license notices. It contains no publisher Google credentials or saved accounts.

Download source ZIP ↗

Source version, size & SHA-256

You can install the normal Windows app without building it yourself. Application code is MIT licensed; SMBLibrary and Utilities are LGPL-3.0-or-later. A Windows build needs .NET SDK 10 and Python 3.11+. Follow README.md and Build.ps1 in the ZIP.

Before your first sign-in: this release has no bundled publisher OAuth registration. Create a Desktop client in your own Google project and import its JSON locally. You do not send it to this website or to support.

1. Create or select your project

Open Google Cloud Console. Click the project selector at the top, then New project, or select your existing project. Keep that project selected for all the following steps.

Cloudlane does not need a VM, storage bucket or service account. A free-trial banner is separate from creating the Drive OAuth client.

2. Enable Google Drive API

Open the console menu → APIs & Services → Library. Search for Google Drive API, open it and click Enable.

3. Configure Google sign-in

Open Google Auth Platform → Overview. If it says the platform is not configured, click Get started. Enter your app name and support/contact email. Choose External for a personal Gmail account and complete the contact and policy steps.

Open Audience → Test users → Add users. Add the exact email you will use to sign in, including your own. Owning the project does not automatically make your email a test user.

Under Data Access, add https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive. Cloudlane uses this permission to browse existing files, stream, upload, rename, create folders and move deleted items to Trash.

Google policies still apply. While your project is in Testing, Drive authorizations normally expire after seven days. Sign in again when needed. Sharing a client with other people may require additional Google configuration or verification.

4. Download your Desktop client JSON

  1. Open Google Auth Platform → Clients.
  2. Click Create client.
  3. Set Application type to Desktop app, enter a name and create it.
  4. Download the JSON from the creation dialog or client details.

The file contains both the client ID and client secret. You do not need to copy them separately. A Web application client, API key or service-account JSON will not work.

5. Import, sign in and connect

  1. Open Cloudlane and click Google app setup.
  2. Click Choose Desktop client JSON and select your downloaded file.
  3. Click Done, then Sign in with Google. Use a test-user email and review the consent screen.
  4. Choose an unused drive letter and click Connect drive. Approve Windows administrator access using the same Windows account.
  5. Click Open in Explorer. Keep Cloudlane running while using the drive.

The imported configuration and saved sign-in tokens use Windows user encryption. The original downloaded JSON remains in your download folder unless you remove it. Add Google account connects additional accounts through the same client; each account authorizes access separately.

Enable each account’s Auto-connect checkbox and Start with Windows if you want to reconnect at startup. Windows approval may still appear.

If something blocks setup

Access blocked: check the selected project and Audience → Test users. Add the exact email shown in Google’s error, then start sign-in again from Cloudlane. Your organization may restrict access.

Replacing a client: disconnect and forget all saved accounts first. Import the replacement and sign in again; existing tokens belong to the old client.

Windows compatibility: the driverless Explorer connection requires Windows 11 24H2 or newer, build 26100+, on x64. Windows 10 and earlier Windows 11 releases are not supported by this release.

For privacy and local data removal, see the Privacy Policy. Official details: Google Desktop OAuth documentation.

Support: support@hisabi.store. Include your app version and relevant diagnostics. Never send client JSON, passwords or account tokens.
